state.instructions: Judge alternatives for finishing the CanLeave and CanShift source examples. No compiler, standard library, adapter or deployed runtime is being supplied. Treat classifications as recommendations, keeping uncertainty visible and leaving user requirements authoritative.
state.facts: The requested behavior includes inclusive calendar-day snapshots and per-year atomic allowance charging. Sick and personal leave should avoid vacation charges except through an explicit configured mapping. Only the owner, HR and the designated location-eligible approver can see private details; shared planning exposes accepted dates. Existing reserve/stage/release operations of ScheduleV1 already use OperationOutcome revisions and release tombstones, with Book/Hire/Field depending on their shapes. Preserve them. Published role coverage must be continuous, substitutes must pass current skills/location/availability checks with travel margins, and revoked employees must cause conflicts and obsolete requests without deleting dependent work. Record notice outcomes and guard delivery against obsolete revisions. EmployeeChanged currently lacks export and occurs only in deactivate, so its owner must expose it and emit for relevant updates before Shift subscribes.

completion.question: Choose the option that most closely satisfies the stated application behavior.

criteria.explicit: Declare Calendar-owned Category policies with an optional allowance_bucket; copy the selected mapping into each Request and retain date Portions whose allowance can be null. Validate window coverage at its beginning and all internal duty endings. Extend the current revisioned schedule with dispatch-guarded notices, correlated reserve/release outcomes and a guarded manager resolution. More fields and policy records are needed, while existing schedule identity and interfaces remain intact.
criteria.minimal: Keep every Portion tied to an Allowance, leave uncharged categories as prose, and count only duties spanning an entire window. Recheck employee permission at new actions without reacting to earlier assignments after revocation. Fewer declarations are added, at the cost of no unmetered date ledger, incomplete reconciliation and no authored notice lifecycle.
